Web search was unavailable this session; discovery ran via outlet site-search and Google News RSS titles, and only opened URLs are cited.

symmetryCheck: Control 1 — Delhi 2002 (a Congress-governed state, verified only as to mechanics): DVB was unbundled on 1 Jul 2002 under a 2000 ordinance and one private group (BSES/Reliance) took 51% of two of the three discoms with the government holding 49%, Tata the third. Control 2 — Odisha's first round (1999, pre-BJD): CESCO's licence was revoked in Apr 2005 and the utility run by the state until Tata Power's 2019–20 win under the same 51:49 template. Applying the 'one group wins most of the privatised assets' lens to these controls produces the same shape as Odisha 2020–21 (Tata took all four discoms) and the UT round (three groups, three deals) — so beneficiary concentration at privatisation is non-discriminating across parties and decades; the discriminating variables are bid margin, criteria changes and litigation outcomes, which for Chandigarh (Rs 871 vs 606 crore, seven bids) point to a genuine auction and for DNH-DD are unknown. The lens also reproduces the bonds pattern for a non-BJP recipient: the largest power-sector bond buyer (Haldia Energy, Rs 377 crore) sits in a TMC-governed state and press reports (not opened) place most of its bonds with TMC. Conclusion: the lens is not specific to the Union government; it flags any incumbent–licensee pair.
